title: MKUltra: The CIA's Declassified Files
summary: CIA Director Helms ordered MKUltra files destroyed in 1973; a 1977 FOIA request surfaced ~20,000 misfiled records. At the Aug 3, 1977 Senate hearings, DCI Stansfield Turner testified on the finds: 149 subprojects across 80+ institutions (universities, hospitals, prisons, pharma companies); unwitting dosing of American and Canadian citizens with LSD and other drugs. Program closed 1964, some work continuing as MKSEARCH.
tldr: This CIA-released document is an Intellipedia article confirming MKULTRA as a real CIA mind-control/chemical-interrogation program begun in the early 1950s under Sidney Gottlieb, with over 150 subprojects, LSD dosing of unwitting subjects — killing at least one, Dr. Frank Olson — and its files destroyed on Helms's 1973 order.
ai_summary:
AI review of CIA Reading Room doc C06760269 — a CIA Intellipedia article on Project MKULTRA, 'Approved for Release: 2018/12/12' (OCR'd PDF, ~6.7k words), read in full:
- 'MK-ULTRA was the code name for a covert CIA mind-control and chemical interrogation research program, run by the Office of Scientific Intelligence,' brought to wide public attention in 1975 via the Church Committee and Rockefeller Commission; Director Richard Helms 'ordered all MK-ULTRA files destroyed in 1973.'
- Started on CIA Director Allen Dulles's order in 1953, headed by Dr. Sidney Gottlieb; precursors Project BLUEBIRD (1950) → ARTICHOKE (1951); renamed MK-SEARCH in 1964; goal included 'a perfect truth drug' and 'Manchurian Candidate'-style mind control. Over 150 individually funded research subprojects; 1955 doc listed targets like illogical thinking, hypnosis enhancement, amnesia, and a 'knockout pill.'
- Money: the director got 'six percent of the CIA' 1953 operating budget; an estimated US$10M or more was spent.
- Senator Ted Kennedy's 1977 Senate-floor statement, quoted in the doc: 'over thirty universities and institutions' were involved in covert drug tests on 'unwitting citizens at all social levels, high and low, native Americans and foreign'; 'At least one death, that of Dr. Frank Olson, resulted from these activities,' and 'The Agency itself acknowledged that these tests made little scientific sense.'
- Note on record-summary accuracy: the doc says 'more than 150' subprojects and 'over thirty' institutions (Kennedy), not the summary's '149 subprojects across 80+ institutions' from the Turner testimony; the 1977 FOIA's ~20,000 surfaced records are not mentioned in this doc. Flagging for the record author.
